mission_05: DBSCAN (Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise) is a clustering algorithm that naturally identifies outliers as points that do not belong to any cluster. Unlike k-means which forces every point into a cluster, DBSCAN classifies points as core points (sufficiently dense neighborhood), border points (reachable from core points), or noise points (outliers). The algorithm requires two parameters: eps defines the neighborhood radius, and min_samples specifies the minimum number of points needed to form a dense region. Points that cannot reach a dense region within eps distance are labeled as noise (-1). DBSCAN excels at finding clusters of arbitrary shape and automatically determining the number of clusters, while simultaneously identifying outliers. It is particularly effective for spatial data, image segmentation, and any dataset where clusters are not spherical.
